title: I made a city manager game in one day, with Claude
author: techbear1980
selftext:
I'm an old, experienced indie game dev.  My buddy finally got me to try Claude Code.  I used Claude to build this reinterpretation of an ancient old city manager game.  This was built in a day, which probably won't surprise you.

It's written using Godot, and the web version is published to itch.io.

\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*

Here's the game description:

Every year, your steward Ishme brings you a report on your city-state: how many people are left, how much grain is in the store, and what the priests expect the river to do next. Then you make the year's decrees:

* **Buy or sell land** at this year's price.
* **Set rations.** Hungry subjects are unhappy subjects. Starving subjects are former subjects.
* **Plant your fields,** if you can spare the seed and the farmers.
* **Put people to work** digging canals or building a granary that the rats can't get into.

Then you end the year, the sun crosses the sky, and you find out how it went. The river floods generously, or barely, or not at all. Rats get into the grain. Newcomers turn up, drawn by tales of your granaries. Keep the people content, or they'll find someone else to be king.

Along the way the priests bring you laws to carve into the stele, and stone is hard to erase. Will you make builders answer for their work with their lives? Forgive everyone's debts? Open a tavern? Each of the 22 laws helps you in one way and costs you in another. Thirteen events, from plagues to visiting scribes, make sure no two reigns go the same way.

At the end of your reign you're judged: a grade from A to F and a title to match. The Records of the Kings keep every reign, so you can look back on your finest hour, or your Grain Goblin era.
